title: NY State Assembly · District 48
area: Borough Park and surrounding neighborhoods of southern Brooklyn.

context.text: Incumbent Simcha Eichenstein is unopposed on the November 3, 2026 general-election ballot. The Democratic and Conservative Party primaries scheduled for June 23, 2026 were both canceled, and no Republican candidate filed.

candidates.name: Simcha Eichenstein

summary.text: Simcha Eichenstein is the Democratic and Conservative Party incumbent running unopposed for re-election. A former aide to New York State Comptroller Thomas DiNapoli and to Mayor Bill de Blasio, he has represented District 48, which includes Borough Park, since 2019, succeeding longtime Assemblyman Dov Hikind. Ballotpedia lists his committees as Cities, Governmental Employees, Housing, Insurance, Real Property Taxation, and Social Services.

background.text: According to his official biography, he is a graduate of New York's yeshiva system and a lifelong resident of Borough Park.
Before elected office, he worked as political affairs director at a public relations firm, as a special assistant in the New York State legislature, and as a member of Brooklyn's Community Board 12.
Served for four years as a senior aide to State Comptroller Thomas P. DiNapoli, working on intergovernmental affairs and relations with community and non-profit organizations.

Worked on Mayor Bill de Blasio's legislative affairs team in Albany and on the mayor's senior intergovernmental staff at City Hall, with a portfolio that included the Department of Health and Mental Hygiene, the Department for the Aging, the Department of Homeless Services and NYC Health + Hospitals.

Elected November 6, 2018, to represent the 48th Assembly District, which his official biography says includes Borough Park, Kensington and Midwood; the biography states he was the first Chassidic Jewish individual elected to the state legislature.
Assumed office in the New York State Assembly on January 1, 2019, succeeding Dov Hikind.
Was appointed Assistant Majority Whip of the Assembly on the first day of the 2023 legislative session.

His official biography lists legislation he sponsored and passed, including exempting Summer Youth Employment Program earnings when calculating household income for public assistance eligibility, requiring state correctional facilities to offer kosher and halal options in commissaries and vending machines, and exempting first responders from monetary penalties for violations committed while responding to medical emergencies.
Has served on the Housing, Cities, Governmental Employees, Real Property Taxation and Social Services committees throughout his tenure, adding the Insurance Committee in the 2025-2026 session.
His official biography states that he and his wife, Pearl, have four children.

priorities.text: Advocating for the Orthodox Jewish community's religious-accommodation needs, such as exempting Sabbath-observant residents from sanitation ticketing on Friday afternoons.
Public safety around houses of worship, community centers and schools.

record.text: Sponsored legislation, with State Senator Sam Sutton, prohibiting the NYC Department of Sanitation from issuing summonses for setting out trash after 3:00 p.m. on Fridays, an accommodation for Sabbath-observant New Yorkers; the bill passed both houses and was signed into law by Governor Kathy Hochul in December 2025.

Was among the Assembly members, along with State Senator Sam Sutton, whose effort secured legislation in the state budget establishing 50-foot buffer zones around houses of worship, community centers and schools, creating misdemeanor penalties for harassment or intimidation within that zone.

Sent a letter to New York Attorney General Letitia James asking her office to review whether NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani's public statements about potentially having New York City law enforcement arrest Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu violated state law.

candidates.researchNotes: Eichenstein is running unopposed. No campaign website was found (he lists only official and personal social-media accounts on Ballotpedia); his record here is drawn from his official nyassembly.gov press releases, Ballotpedia's biography/committee data, and the assembly-ny.json roll-call snapshot. No documented statement was found linking him directly to a position on any of the fixed issue-list statements without inferring beyond what he said, so the positions list is empty.
